name: Lubbard Fiend

attributes.attribute: described by John Milton in L'Allegro
a helpful brownie or lubber seen through Puritan eyes

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The Lubbard Fiend is a folkloric figure of Britain. The poet John Milton names it in his work L'Allegro. Milton writes of a drudging goblin that threshed corn that ten day-laborers could not finish, then slept by the fire to recover from its work until dawn, when it vanished. Though the figure appears nowhere else, it seems a friendly brownie or a lubber of the sort described under Lob. The strict Puritan language of his age led Milton to write of the helpful fairy farmhand in a sour way.

okr.objective: Document the Lubbard Fiend as a British folk figure recorded by John Milton.
